text:
maya: Heads-up — found a weird parse crash in the browser sample app when the client disconnects mid-stream, feels like a half-chunk gets handed to the JSON parser and it explodes.

jonah: Ugh. Which sample app and which SDK? Browser or node?

maya: The quickstart fetch-based streaming example (react sample). Happens in Chrome -> later repro in Safari too. Node sample using EventSource doesn't hit it.

samir: Can you paste the error/log? Might be our SSE framing boundary assumption.

maya: Sure. Repro steps: start sample, call streaming chat, then close tab ~200ms after first chunk. Server logs show a flushed buffer and client sees: \n```
Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
 at parse (<anonymous>)
 at onmessage (stream-parser.js:42)
```
Client-side capture shows last recv chunk: `{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"So you can use `"` (truncated)
```

jonah: Looks like truncated UTF-8 + JSON boundary. Our browser-side `fetch().body.getReader()` code concatenates chunks and tries to parse each time it sees a `\n\n` delimiter, but the tab close triggers an abrupt `close()` event where the final CRLF isn’t delivered.

devex-team: Adding to triage. Two angles: make parser tolerant (ignore trailing partial JSON on connection close) and make server emit an explicit final boundary before closing. Which is easier short-term?

samir: Parser change is safest client-side. On close, treat remaining buffer as "incomplete" and drop (log metric). Server change requires changing streaming runtime flush behavior and could break other clients.

maya: I hacked the react sample to only parse strict full JSON objects and ignore partials on `reader.closed` — fixed the crash but the UI shows truncated last message. Patch attached: \n```
// simplified pseudo
while(true) {
 const {done, value} = await reader.read()
 if (done) break
 buf += decoder.decode(value, {stream: true})
 let parts = buf.split('\n\n')
 for (let i=0;i<parts.length-1;i++) handleJSON(parse(parts[i]))
 buf = parts[parts.length-1]
}
// on done: drop buf if not valid JSON
```

jonah: That seems fine. We should also consider auth token rotation mid-stream — we saw reports where the SDK would try an automatic retry and end up duplicating last chunk because server replays prefix. Any chance that's related?

samir: Different root cause but could surface similarly. When a 401 occurs mid-stream our proxy aborts and the client-side retry logic can re-request and get overlapping fragments. We need a simple idempotency token or resume-offset header for streaming replays.

devex-team: Action items:
- samir: open infra ticket to avoid auto-flush-without-boundary on abrupt disconnect (low priority) — ref #INF-4627
- jonah: add a tolerant parser option to browser SDK and a demo fix in samples (high priority)
- maya: drop a minimal repro gist and add exact browser versions + steps
- devex-team: scope a longer design for stream resume semantics (idempotency token / resume cursor)

maya: I uploaded a gist: https://gist.github.com/maya/stream-trunc-repro

jonah: I'll PR the SDK patch tomorrow, will follow the "tolerant parsing" approach and add an opt-in flag `allowPartialStreamOnClose` default false.

infra-bot: Note: created INF-4627, linked to thread 1999001111.

maya: Thanks — assigning to you @jonah, and cc @samir for infra follow-up. :thumbsup:
